  "hypothesis": "Predicted that the intervention training would improve the number of correct decisions to shoot in shoot scenarios and to not shoot in don't shoot scenarios to a greater extent than the control group.",
  "design": "mixed, 2 (group: intervention vs. control) x 2 (measurement time: pre-test vs. post-test)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "An individual video-based police firearms training intervention based on the Four-Component Instructional Design Model (4C/ID), focusing on situational awareness, tactical gaze control, and visual attention, compared to an active control training resembling traditional police firearms training.",
  "outcome_measure": "Correctness of shoot/don't shoot decisions in realistic video scenarios.",
  "population_and_setting": "45 senior police officers at the German Police University, tested in an indoor firing range lab setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 45,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via notices on campus; participation was voluntary.",
  "analysis_plan": "Non-parametric Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test to compare the progress (post-test minus pre-test) of correct decisions between the intervention and control groups.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "preregistered",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants were randomly allocated to groups. Both groups watched an educational video before practical training. The study used a gas-operated replica handgun.
